title_jp: {防災庁|ぼうさいちょう}{発足|ほっそく}
context: News from 2 November 2026: Japan opened a new government agency for disasters, the 防災庁. On day one it asked everyone to store at least 3 days of water and food, ideally a week. Useful words for anyone staying in an earthquake country.

phrases.jp: {水|みず}と{食料|しょくりょう}を{備蓄|びちく}しておきましょう。
phrases.en: Let's stock up on water and food.
phrases.note: {備蓄|びちく} = stockpile. ～ておく = do something in advance.

phrases.jp: {最低|さいてい}3{日分|みっかぶん}、できれば1{週間分|しゅうかんぶん}です。
phrases.en: At least 3 days' worth, ideally a week's.
phrases.note: ～{分|ぶん} = "worth of": 3{日分|みっかぶん}, 2{人分|ふたりぶん}.

phrases.jp: {避難所|ひなんじょ}はどこですか。
{地震|じしん}のとき、どうすればいいですか。
phrases.en: What should I do in an earthquake?

phrases.jp: {水|みず}、{何|なん}リットル{買|か}えばいい？
phrases.en: How many litres of water should we buy?

dialogue_setting: At home, your host is watching the evening news.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.jp: ニュース{見|み}た？{今週|こんしゅう}、{防災庁|ぼうさいちょう}ができたんだって。
dialogue.en: Did you see the news? A disaster agency was set up this week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: {防災庁|ぼうさいちょう}？{何|なに}をするところですか。
dialogue.en: A disaster agency? What does it do?

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.jp: {地震|じしん}とか{災害|さいがい}の{準備|じゅんび}。{家|いえ}に1{週間分|しゅうかんぶん}の{水|みず}と{食料|しょくりょう}を{用意|ようい}してって。
dialogue.en: It prepares for earthquakes and disasters. They're asking us to keep a week of water and food at home.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: 1{週間分|しゅうかんぶん}ですか。この{家|いえ}は{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}ですか。
dialogue.en: A week's worth? Is this house OK?

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.jp: {水|みず}がちょっと{少|すく}ないかな。{明日|あした}、{一緒|いっしょ}に{買|か}いに{行|い}こう。
dialogue.en: We're a bit short on water. Let's go and buy some together tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: はい、{手伝|てつだ}います！

kanji.where: On signs at schools, community centres and parks: where to go after a big earthquake. Find the nearest one to where you're staying on your first day.
kanji.related: Related: {避難場所|ひなんばしょ} evacuation area, {非常口|ひじょうぐち} emergency exit.

tip.title: The 3-litre rule
tip.body: The guideline is 3 litres of water per person per day, including cooking, so one week for one person is 21 litres. Many families use "rolling stock" (ローリングストック): buy a bit extra of what you normally eat and use the oldest first. On your stay, ask your host where the emergency bag ({非常持|ひじょうも}ち{出|だ}し{袋|ぶくろ}) is.

challenge.prompt: Ask your host: "Where is the nearest evacuation shelter?"
challenge.hint: nearest = {一番|いちばん}{近|ちか}い
challenge.model_answer: {一番|いちばん}{近|ちか}い{避難所|ひなんじょ}はどこですか。
